title: Good gh-ost invocation — correct operation mode for large-table type change
migration_snippet:
# Migration plan: user_id INT -> BIGINT on events (80M rows)
# Mode (a): --host is a REPLICA, so --allow-on-master is NOT used.
# Step 1: dry-run (omit --execute)
gh-ost --host=replica1.db.internal --port=3306 \
  --database=app --table=events \
  --alter='MODIFY COLUMN user_id BIGINT NOT NULL' \
  --chunk-size=1000 --max-lag-millis=1500 \
  --max-load=Threads_running=25 --critical-load=Threads_running=1000 \
  --throttle-control-replicas='replica1.db.internal:3306,replica2.db.internal:3306' \
  --exact-rowcount --concurrent-rowcount \
  --postpone-cut-over-flag-file=/tmp/ghost.postpone.flag \
  --panic-flag-file=/tmp/ghost.panic.flag

# Step 2: re-run with --execute; copy runs, then waits at the postpone flag
# Step 3: verify, then delete the postpone flag to cut over
# Step 4: keep _events_old until the rollback window closes (no --ok-to-drop-table)
# SELECT COLUMN_TYPE FROM information_schema.COLUMNS
#  WHERE TABLE_NAME='events' AND COLUMN_NAME='user_id';
expected_feedback: No violations. INT->BIGINT is a data-type change, which the manual supports only with ALGORITHM=COPY — unsafe at 80M rows, so gh-ost is the right tool. The invocation uses gh-ost's default mode (--host is a replica) and correctly omits --allow-on-master, which is the opt-in for pointing gh-ost at the master. Dry-run precedes --execute; load and lag throttles are set; cut-over is postponed behind a flag file; no destructive cleanup flag is present, so the _old table survives as the rollback path.
